title: Table rewrite happens when increasing a varchar length past 63

comments.text:
Hi Mr. ODonell,

Thank you very much for your bug report.

However, this is documented.  We suppose you used InnoDB storage engine.

The problem is in the magical number of 255. With a default character set, VARCHAR(64) is larger then 255 bytes. Hence, for 256 until 65535 bytes of length, you require two bytes for the actual length of the string. Hence , that is why a rebuild is necessary. To add one more byte for the actual length of the variable-length strings.

Not a bug.

Hi,

It is actually explained in our Manual:

https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/char.html

in the first 4-5 paragraphs.

I think https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/9.1/en/innodb-online-ddl-operations.html#online-ddl-colum... could be improved by adding an asterisk to the "Yes" under "Permits Concurrent DML" for "Extending VARCHAR column size," as happens in "Adding a column," for example. 

While it is true the existing documentation explains this behaviour, I still think that table is misleading and can be improved with this simple change.
